note: Frozen VERIFY verdicts + exit codes ONLY (no obligation-report/trust-report/classification fields, the standing A3-churn guard). driver-spec.txt section 15.1 (proved tier) and section 15.2 (asserted tier). Six of the cruxes are defects that actually shipped or behaviour the Python driver still has, not invented mutants; each names its provenance in `why`. This suite is addressed by repo-relative path and each case is verified against a copy of the whole directory, because shell.llmll and crux-shell-undeclared-authority.llmll import sibling modules; `verify` still checks only the named file, so the extra siblings change no verdict. The `capability` expectation is the third verdict kind: a capability violation is neither `safe` nor `refuted`, and grading it as `refuted` meant a program rejected at type-check stood in for one the solver disproved. Extended at v0.14.82 by the DRIVER-LL Phase 3 port with spine.llmll and crux-stage-j-coverage-pin.llmll: before that pair neither stage E's nor stage J's verify verdict was frozen anywhere, so the ported spine was the only unprotected artifact in a directory whose whole point is frozen verdicts. Extended again by DRIVER-LL Phase 4 sub-phase 4a with registry.llmll, manifest.llmll, sequencer.llmll and two cruxes. crux-exit-code-halt-as-zero.llmll is what raises the shipped-behaviour count from five to six: exiting 0 on a halted run is what EVERY LLMLL console program did before PROC-BOUNDARY-1, since the harness had no status channel at all. crux-skip-digest-dropped.llmll is an INVENTED mutant and is the discriminating half of proposal section 10 case 19: it refutes [S5-SKIP] and NOT [S5-PRESENCE], where crux-skip-presence-only.llmll refutes both, so the pair makes the entailment observable in the gate rather than only argued. Extended again by sub-phase 4b with validate.llmll and two cruxes. validate.llmll is the delegated-output validation facility of driver-spec section 7:283-291, and its verdict is frozen because both of its functions are body-faithful and both carry postconditions that a later widening could silently drop. crux-validate-downgrade.llmll is the WARNING DOWNGRADE section 7:283-286 forbids, and it refutes through [V7-MANDATORY] ALONE: measured, the same body carrying [V7-PASS] plus [V7-ONLY-TWO] is SAFE, because Finished is one of the two constructors [V7-ONLY-TWO] admits. crux-validate-subject-hardcoded.llmll is an INVENTED MUTANT and the discriminating half of section 7:288-291: its `(> size floor)` guard is what keeps it from ALSO refuting [V7-FLOOR], measured, so the mutant refutes through the anti-hardcoding post and not through a post about floors.

section 15.2 asserted tier: every effect reached through a declared capability or the Host interface; each function's authority is minimal and finish-stage inherits the union of its callees

DRIVER-LL Phase 3, stages E and J. The verdict being frozen is the split: five defs body-faithful (stage-e-passes, stage-e-outcome, stage-j-pins, bad-barrier-count, stage-j-outcome) and the def-shell orchestration around them at body-fallback. No `--strict-verified-core`, because the shell layer is the asserted tier by construction; what the frozen verdict protects is that the proved centre stays SAFE and that the module keeps importing stage/skip/gate rather than reimplementing their decisions

DRIVER-LL Phase 4a, the sixteen-stage table. No `def` at all, so the frozen verdict protects compile-ability and the import surface rather than a proof: what would break it is a paren-count drift in one of the five if-chains, which is exactly the failure mode a hand-written table has
DRIVER-LL Phase 4a, the row schema and the corrupt-manifest guard. Imports stage for Status and Outcome, so it is a cross-module case

DRIVER-LL Phase 4a, the stage loop. The frozen verdict protects the split: exit-code is body-faithful and carries the five posts that tie the process status to the proved halt classification, while the orchestration around it is def-shell at body-fallback. No --strict-verified-core, on spine.llmll's precedent, because the shell layer is the asserted tier by construction; what this guards is that the proved centre stays SAFE and that the module keeps importing skip and stage rather than reimplementing their decisions

DRIVER-LL Phase 4b, the delegated-output validation facility. Both verdict-of and verdict-outcome are body-faithful. Frozen because the acceptance clause of sub-phase 4b -- an output that is absent, malformed or subject-hardcoded fails the stage -- is carried by these two functions' postconditions and by nothing else in the port; a widening that dropped one would leave every cover cell green, since the cover drives the same code it would be checking.

INVENTED MUTANT, and the discriminating half of proposal section 10 case 19: the digest conjunct dropped rather than the presence conjunct. [S5-SKIP] refutes and [S5-PRESENCE] does not. MEASURED at v0.14.84: the same body carrying ONLY [S5-PRESENCE] verifies SAFE, which is the entailment CLAUSE-INDEP-1 is filed against made observable

SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR: before PROC-BOUNDARY-1 every LLMLL console program exited 0 on the :done? path whatever it had decided, so a driver that halted at a gate and one that finished every stage were indistinguishable to a shell. Stopped mapped to 0 is that behaviour narrowed to the arm where it matters; [EXIT-STOPPED] and [EXIT-NOVACUOUS] both refute it

section 15.2: writes the filesystem while importing only wasi.io. Fails at TYPE-CHECK, not at the solver, which is the point: authority is enforced rather than declared. Graded under the `capability` expectation, which matches the missing-capability diagnostic; `refuted` would have accepted any error at all and is now explicitly rejected for this case.

THE WARNING DOWNGRADE driver-spec section 7:283-286 forbids: an output that failed validation let through as though it had passed. Absent, the arm section 7:279 names ('silence is not success'), is mapped to Finished. Refutes [V7-MANDATORY] alone; measured, the same body carrying every other post is SAFE.

INVENTED MUTANT: the validator driver-spec section 7:288-291 warns about, accepting exactly the one size a committed run produced. The (> size floor) guard makes it discriminating: with the guard it satisfies [V7-PRESENCE] and [V7-FLOOR] and refutes [V7-NO-HARDCODE] and its named consequence [V7-NO-FLOOR]; without it, it also refutes [V7-FLOOR] and would have been a mutant about floors wearing an anti-hardcoding label. Measured both ways.

DRIVER-LL Phase 4c, the content-shape validation channel validate.llmll:56-63 reserved by name. All FOUR functions are body-faithful, which is the property the frozen verdict protects and which is not free: both regexes these validators need are portable (regex-match is a compiler builtin) but LLMLL.md:326 puts regex-match outside Sigma_auto and LLMLL.md:356 states the consequence, that the carrying function falls to erBodyFallback. Every parameter here is a bool or an int precisely so the regexes stay in the def-shell extractor and the proved core stays in QF-LIA. A later widening that let a Json or a string into any of these signatures would silently forfeit the body-faithful claim for the whole module, and this verdict is what catches it. Takes --strict-verified-core, unlike sequencer.llmll and spine.llmll, because there is no shell layer here at all.

INVENTED MUTANT, and the anti-hardcoding half of the 4c pair. Fitted to 119, the normative row count of the committed experiments/rfc-swarm/data/extraction-a.json. It needs no second run to fail: stage D runs TWO blind extractors and the committed pair disagrees on census size, A having 119 rows and B having 125, so a validator fitted to A rejects extractor B inside the SAME run. MEASURED at v0.14.87: the four forward posts together are SAFE over this body, because it is strictly STRONGER than the honest decision, and [D7-NO-HARDCODE] alone refutes. No forward post can catch a validator that rejects conforming input, which is why the converse post exists.

INVENTED MUTANT, and the other half of the pair: check_extraction's five per-row clauses dropped while the envelope clauses stay. The clause guards the NEXT stage's input rather than this stage's tidiness, since reconcile.py matches by line span and :407's own message says so, and a census with a string line_start reaching stage E gets arithmetic done on it. MEASURED at v0.14.87: everything except [D7-ROWS], INCLUDING [D7-NO-HARDCODE], is SAFE over this body, because it is strictly WEAKER than the honest decision; [D7-ROWS] alone refutes. The pair is what covers both directions, a forward post catching a validator that accepts too much and the converse catching one that accepts too little.

driver-spec section 6:229-231 not enforced: a body answering true whatever the counts, so an exclusion citing a barrier outside the closed list reaches gate J. This is the ONE spec-defined halt in stage G (rfc_to_implementation.py:493 raises it through require_spec, not require), which is why it records `stopped` and why it does not route through validate.verdict-outcome, whose [V7-NO-STOP] forbids ConditionUnmet. NOT a discriminating mutant and does not claim to be: MEASURED at v0.14.87, both [G6-CLOSED] and [G6-NOVACUOUS] refute, because [G6-CLOSED] is an equality between two booleans and so determines result entirely, making the other a named consequence in the sense [V7-NO-FLOOR] is one and gate.llmll's [S6-REPORTED] is one. The cost of a vacuous check here is auditability rather than safety: gate J still holds, but the stage-level halt disappears and a run stops at J with no record of which stage produced the row.
